newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares end firm, led by low-price stocks.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares end firm, led by low-price stocks.

text.p: The Singapore stock market got a lift from improved sentiment, notably in low-priced stocks, and ended firmer in active trade on Wednesday, dealers said.
"It's a mixture of improved sentiment and technicals," one dealer said, adding that weak economic news had been factored in by investors, who were hoping for a rebound in the market.
"The play is mostly on small cap and low priced stocks," another dealer said. "These stocks are relatively cheaper compared to Malaysian second-board stocks."
The key Straits Times Industrials Index closed 7.61 points higher at 2,046.45.
Turnover was active around 210 million shares, with gainers leading losers by 290 to 80.
Newly listed SMB United topped the actives with 18.4 million shares. It was followed by Advanced Systems Automation and Labroy Marine with 17.5 million and 13.6 million shares respectively.
Index stock City Developments was among the gainers, rising S$0.40 to S$11.00. UOE Ltd was among the losers, shedding S$0.20 to S$6.80.
Dealers said they would watch Thursday's performance to see if the market rally was sustainable. -- Angela Tan (65 8703083)
